full_citation: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation (2024). Radioactive Effluents from Nuclear Power Plants, Annual Report 2021. NUREG/CR-2907, Volume 27. ADAMS ML24134A119.
notes: CORRECTS EXISTING ROW S0121. FULL TEXT READ (98 pp, PDF supplied by Steve; text layer parsed). Tables 3-1 to 3-14 (per-reactor, significant nuclides, Ci) and 3-15/3-16 (all noble gases per reactor, 2017-2021) and 3-17/3-18 (all MFAP per reactor, mCi). 93 operating reactors in 2021 (31 BWR, 62 PWR). Multi-unit sites are split equally between units unless the licensee reports otherwise (p.1-5), so sums are valid but unit values are not. Blank cell = not detected (treated as zero in medians). The noble-gas Tables 3-1/3-6 list only Kr-85, Xe-133, Xe-135 and so UNDERSTATE total noble gas by about 3x (BWR) and 1.5x (PWR); use Tables 3-15/3-16 for the all-nuclide figure (BWR median 21.0 Ci, PWR median 1.0 Ci per reactor in 2021). Fleet sums computed by the round-2 researcher: see research/nuclear/papers_round2.md section 2. Long-term trend: BWR median noble gas more than 40,000 Ci in 1975 vs 21.0 Ci in 2021; BWR median liquid MFAP more than 1,500 mCi in 1975 vs 1.5 mCi in 2021. Reported effluents include licensee ESTIMATES (notably C-14).

notes: CORRECTS EXISTING ROW S0138 (was inaccessible). READ from PDFs supplied by Steve (OCR text layer; digits sometimes spaced). Vol. I ch. 9 (printed p.152): about 2.5 million curies of noble gases and 15 curies of radioiodines released. Vol. II Pt 2, Table II-1 (printed p.344): release by nuclide Kr-88 3.75e5 Ci, Xe-133 1.58e6 Ci, Xe-133m 2.25e5 Ci, Xe-135 3.0e5 Ci, Xe-135m 2.5e4 Ci, I-131 15 Ci (core inventory at shutdown Xe-133 1.42e8 Ci, I-131 6.55e7 Ci, Kr-88 6.92e7, Xe-133m 2.11e7, Xe-135 3.31e7, Xe-135m 2.60e7). Table 11-3 (pp.355-357): cumulative I-131 14.56 Ci through 8 May 1979; Tables 11-4/11-5: 32 Ci (95% RH, upper bound, high by factor 2-3) and 17 Ci (30% RH). Sect. 11 (pp.358-360): TLD back-calculation 13e6 Ci (as Xe-133) and a second TLD method 10e6 Ci (Xe-133 8.3e6, Xe-133m 1.5e6, others <2e5); Rogovin finds the 2.5 MCi term the best estimate because it extrapolates measured releases near the source. Rogovin states Kr-85 and Kr-87 were NOT released in significant quantity during the accident; about 50,000 Ci of Kr-85 remained in containment six months later (p.360). Vol. II p1-p3 searched for release data (nothing further found).
